name: Capability-Bundle Mismatch Law Candidate
claim_form: When an existing abstraction requires capabilities not required by a newly admitted implementation demand, reusing that abstraction can impose conformance burden or semantic overclaim. Capability segregation can reduce that burden, but only when the coordination cost of splitting the boundary is repaid and existing behavior remains valid.
falsifiers_or_boundary_evidence: wide-boundary reuse satisfies both real demands without extra capability work, stubs, false capability exposure or later propagation burden
capability segregation adds more authority surfaces and churn without reducing conformance burden
the apparent mismatch disappears when the real product contract is shown to require fetch as well as search
authentication heterogeneity, not capability bundling, explains the measured lifecycle differences
relation_to_SOLID: ISP/OCP/DIP are competing intervention families whose prescriptions may conflict. No principle is treated as an axiom.
